question: Can the 2023 LWR paper be treated as independent supporting fish evidence alongside the 2024 Talisay/Bagac survey and the 2025 three-river survey?

method.procedure: Reviewed the publisher-hosted 2023 six-page PDF in full and compared its authorship, field period, waterbody scope, site descriptions, table scope, specimen-handling notes, figures, and license with the existing 2024 cross-study review and 2025 river-table review.
method.limits: Publication-lineage and source-quality review only; no fish identities, complete inventory, current presence, geometry, or reuse rights were independently established.

publications.citation: Corpuz, M. N. C., Nacorda, H. M. E., Casal, C. M. E., Faustino-Eslava, D. V., Jaranilla-Sanchez, P. A., Vedra, S. A., Paguia, H. M., & Espaldon, M. V. O. (2023). Length-Weight Relationship and Relative Condition Factor of Fishes in Talisay and Bagac River Systems, Bataan, Philippines. International Journal of Latest Engineering Science, 6(4), 12-17. https://doi.org/10.51386/25816659/ijles-v6i4p102.
publications.reportedSampling: The methods say specimens were collected every three months from February through November 2021 with help from local fisherfolk. Captured fish were counted, identified to the lowest possible taxon, held at Bataan Peninsula State University for analysis, and preserved in 10% buffered formaldehyde for further documentation and identification.
publications.tableScope: Table 1 gives sample sizes for 12 unique source-reported taxa across six Talisay and eight Bagac taxon-river rows. It is a selected length-weight/condition-factor analysis, not a complete inventory or station-resolved occurrence matrix.
publications.localityFinding: The body describes Talisay and Bagac rivers, but Figure 1 caption identifies site A as Tagumpay in Orani and site B as Parang in Bagac. The reviewed article supplies no site-to-river or station-to-taxon crosswalk resolving the Talisay/Orani caption discrepancy.
publications.specimenAndImageFinding: No voucher/catalog accession, specimen identifier, sequence accession, or diagnostic fish-photo plate was found in the article. Figures are a site map and condition-factor graphs. The statement that specimens were held/preserved does not prove accessible vouchers remain or identify any table row.
publications.internalTextFlag: The discussion calls some Bagac relationships positive allometric but gives the parenthetical criterion b < 3, while the article defines positive allometry as b > 3. Growth-category prose is internally inconsistent and is not adopted here.
publications.license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, as printed in the PDF footer. No article table, figure, image, or raw species table is reproduced in the app or redistributed by this review.
publications.studyFindingUse: Historical source-reported analysis context only; not independent taxonomic confirmation, current presence, a complete checklist, or fish-image evidence.

publications.citation: Corpuz et al. (2024), Biodiversity Journal, 15(3), 649-658. DOI: 10.31396/Biodiv.Jour.2024.15.3.649.658.
publications.reportedSampling: December 2020 through November 2021; the existing review records nine stations per river and unreconciled internal richness/table statements.
publications.reuseStatus: Existing review did not verify item-specific table reuse terms; rows remain held.
CC BY 4.0; existing review holds all 52 table rows pending overall identity and locality review.

2023vs2024.periodRelationship: The stated February-November 2021 2023 sampling falls within the 2024 December 2020-November 2021 period.
2023vs2024.assessment: Complete author overlap, same rivers, overlapping field window, and specimen-analysis subject make shared project/sample lineage plausible. No specimen, catch, date, or station crosswalk proves overlap or independence.

2024vs2025.periodRelationship: The papers report non-overlapping sampling periods: December 2020-November 2021 and December 2021-November 2022.
2024vs2025.assessment: The exact repeated Talisay and Bagac totals across the two stated non-overlapping survey periods are an unresolved aggregate-lineage/reporting flag. They may reflect coincidence, reused or carried-forward totals, or a reporting error; the reviewed papers do not distinguish these explanations. This is not evidence of misconduct and does not prove duplicated samples.

2023vs2025.periodRelationship: The 2023 stated sampling ends in November 2021; the 2025 paper reports December 2021-November 2022.
2023vs2025.assessment: Author and river overlap links the publications as a research program, but no event-level records show whether the 2023 selected LWR samples were reused, excluded, or independent of either later report.

lineageAssessment.overallConclusion: Keep each publication’s reported sampling window and counts separate. Do not add totals together, use one paper as independent validation of another, or resolve the matching 2024/2025 river totals without author field logs or an explicit sample crosswalk.

evidenceLimits: The 2023 table is a selected length-weight/condition-factor analysis and cannot stand in for a whole-river or provincial inventory.
Figure 1’s Tagumpay-in-Orani label conflicts with the article body’s Talisay River framing; no site crosswalk was published in the reviewed PDF.
No specimen identifiers, museum accessions, DNA accessions, or diagnostic fish-photo plate was located in the reviewed 2023 PDF.
The publisher marks the 2023 item CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. This review makes no legal determination about separate factual extraction; no app reuse or publication is approved.

The 2024 and 2025 papers report the same Talisay (472) and Bagac (505) totals despite different stated sampling windows. Preserve these as separate source-reported values and an unresolved QA signal only.
No paper in this review establishes present-day presence, abundance, catchability, diet, legality, safety, or verified waterway geometry.
nextActions: Ask the corresponding authors for dated field logs, station/catch identifiers, raw per-river/per-event counts, specimen inventories, and an explicit crosswalk for the 2023, 2024, and 2025 outputs; specifically ask them to explain the identical 2024/2025 Talisay and Bagac totals.

Request clarification of the 2023 Figure 1 site A caption (Tagumpay in Orani) against the body’s Talisay River description and obtain the original site list/map coordinates before assigning that sample to a waterbody.
If specimens remain, seek museum or institutional accession numbers and diagnostic images tied to individual records before a separate identity review.
Keep existing Bataan species rows source-reported and research-only; do not admit, deduplicate, or promote rows based on author overlap or matching totals.

Primary methods, Table 1 scope, specimen handling, Figure 1 caption, internal text flag, figures, and CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 notice.
